appearance_facts.fact: Large bold heading reads 'Reduced Screening Referrals Across Hospitals from 2012 to 2023'. A smaller gray subtitle below reads 'Referral-monitoring record shown in the dashboard summary'. The title's wording ('Reduced') conflicts with the line's overall upward movement.

A single orange line connects yearly points from 2012 (left) to 2023 (right). The line begins low (~1,200), rises with a mid-period dip in 2015, climbs steeply from 2020 to a peak at 2022, then dips slightly at 2023.
Y-axis labeled 'Screening referrals' with horizontal gridlines at 0, 800, 1600, 2400, 3200. The 2022 peak sits above the 3200 line; the 2023 point sits just above 3200.
X-axis labeled 'Year' with tick labels 2012 through 2023 in one-year increments.

printed_facts.fact: Chart title states 'Reduced Screening Referrals Across Hospitals from 2012 to 2023', which contradicts the plotted increase from ~1,200 (2012) to ~3,300 (2023).

public_definitions: Page instruction: 'Use the dashboard as the evidence source for selecting the appropriate screening referral follow-up pathway.'
Page instruction: 'Review the screening referral dashboard and assign this record to the operational follow-up pathway that best fits the referral pattern over the reporting period.'
uncertain: The chart title says 'Reduced' but the line clearly increases over the period; it is unclear whether the title is a mislabel or whether the routing should follow the title's semantic claim versus the plotted data.

No explicit threshold or rule maps a numeric pattern (e.g., increase vs. decrease) to the three pathway options; the mapping of 'growth-focused' vs 'reduction-focused' vs 'standard' to the data trend is not defined in the supplied text.
